# Create Ad Creatives with AI

Develop truthful ad directions, editable visual candidates, and a clear comparison for a future test.

[Start this course on AILesson](https://ailesson.io/courses/create-ad-creatives-with-ai)

You have a product to promote, but “make a good ad” leaves several decisions open: what to say, how to show it, and what to learn from the next version. AI can help you develop alternatives and produce files you can change. You still need to check the claims and distinguish an appealing design from evidence of better results.

Work through three self-contained tasks: turn supplied product facts into two message directions, create two visual candidates with editable words, and prepare a comparison with a specific future test hypothesis. Take the Lessons in order for a complete introduction, or choose the task you need. Every Lesson supplies its own practice material.

You will inspect recorded AI results, assemble short requests, and make checks against the original brief. The examples use a synthetic desk organizer and graphic illustrations. Downloadable direction sheets, SVG layouts, PNG previews and worksheets let you restart with your own material.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need an ad account or a design tool?

No account or external software is needed for the recorded exercises. To make your own layouts afterward, use an AI assistant that can produce SVG and PNG files, or an editor that preserves SVG text. This Course does not walk through ad buying or campaign setup.

### Will the images be ready for every advertising platform?

The examples use an internal square design brief, not a platform specification. Before using your own creative, check the destination's current dimensions, file rules, placement preview and linked destination. The drawn call to action is part of the image, not a clickable button.

### Will I know which ad performs better?

You will know how to compare visible features and state a testable idea. The Course contains no live campaign data and does not identify a conversion winner. Any real experiment needs a separate owner and measurement plan.
